name: Vancomycin
route_note: IV infusion (slowly, to avoid infusion reactions) with therapeutic drug monitoring; oral capsules or solution act only in the gut for C. difficile.
targets: D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of peptidoglycan precursors (lipid II)

discovery.note: Isolated from Amycolatopsis orientalis (then Streptomyces orientalis) in a soil sample collected in Borneo by a missionary.

tagline: Glycopeptide workhorse against MRSA and, orally, against C. difficile
summary: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic discovered by Eli Lilly in the 1950s. Once sidelined by toxicity concerns, it became the standard treatment for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and other resistant Gram-positive infections, and oral vancomycin treats Clostridioides difficile colitis.
mechanism: Vancomycin binds through five hydrogen bonds to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of lipid II and nascent peptidoglycan, sterically blocking transglycosylation and transpeptidation and thus cell-wall synthesis in Gram-positive bacteria. It is too large to cross the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria.

Enterococci carrying vanA or vanB gene clusters replace the terminal D-Ala with D-lactate, reducing binding about 1000-fold; vanA transfer to S. aureus produces rare vancomycin-resistant S. aureus (VRSA).
uses: MRSA infections: bacteraemia, endocarditis, pneumonia, osteomyelitis, skin infections
Empirical therapy of serious Gram-positive infections and meningitis (with a cephalosporin)
Infections in patients allergic to beta-lactams
Surgical prophylaxis where MRSA risk is high

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Eli Lilly's E. C. Kornfeld isolates compound 05865 from Bornean soil; it is named after 'vanquish'.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Vancocin; early impure preparations ('Mississippi mud') are associated with toxicity.

history.title: VRE
history.detail: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci are reported in Europe (published 1988).

history.title: VRSA
history.detail: The first clinical vancomycin-resistant S. aureus isolate is identified in Michigan, USA.

history.title: WHO Watch group
history.detail: Vancomycin is classified as a Watch antibiotic on the WHO Essential Medicines List.

history.title: AUC-guided dosing
history.detail: Revised US consensus guidelines (ASHP, IDSA, PIDS, SIDP) recommend AUC-guided rather than trough-only dosing for serious MRSA infection.

pk.half_life: about 4–6 hours with normal renal function

common: Vancomycin infusion reaction (flushing, pruritus, formerly 'red man syndrome')
serious: Acute kidney injury (higher with high troughs and with piperacillin/tazobactam)
DRESS and other severe cutaneous reactions

facts: Vancomycin infusion reaction is a histamine-release phenomenon linked to infusion rate, not true allergy.
The 2020 US guideline recommends targeting an AUC/MIC of 400–600 for serious MRSA infections.
